source.title: Finding the Needle in the Haystack with Convolutions: on the benefits of architectural bias
source.authors: Stéphane d'Ascoli; Levent Sagun; Joan Bruna; G. Biroli

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper and supplemental material; no material cutoff or garbling affects the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the convolutional architectural-bias version by embedding CNN checkpoints into fully connected space, then comparing their performance with CNN and standard FCN baselines.
record.gate_note: The study tests a CNN-to-FCN relaxation protocol. It does not test FCNs trained from scratch with learned sparse local connections. Its CIFAR-10 experiment has no data augmentation, weight decay, or momentum.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares CNNs, FCNs trained from scratch, and FCNs initialized from CNN checkpoints, testing V3 through constraint relaxation. It is an original source for V3, so no verdict labels are assigned.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that convolutional initialization and early constrained training guide optimization toward well-generalizing regions that standard FCN training misses. Relaxation at suitable times can improve on the source CNN while locality remains approximately preserved. They also emphasize that the very large eFCNs make the protocol impractical.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a CNN-to-FCN embedding and staged constraint relaxation, rather than comparing only CNNs and FCNs trained from scratch. It also reports AlexNet on CIFAR-100 in the supplement.
record.method_sensitivity: Relax time changes the outcome: intermediate relaxation can exceed the CNN, while late relaxation leaves accuracy at the CNN level. Optimizer and dataset also vary in the supplemental experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy rises during training after convolutional constraints are relaxed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relaxing convolutional constraints need not cause declining held-out accuracy during subsequent FCN training.

fits_no_version.finding: The off-local weight ratio remains at most 8% for the main eFCNs, compared with about 97% for a standard FCN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional locality can persist approximately under unconstrained SGD after convolutional initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient norm and the largest Hessian eigenvalue fall by roughly an order of magnitude after eFCN training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relaxing convolutional constraints can reduce these landscape indicators without a corresponding large change in test accuracy.

record.problems: The main experiment is on CIFAR-10 without data augmentation and uses a simple three-layer CNN. The paper notes that the eFCN is very large and its protocol is impractical. The text gives differing approximate standard-FCN accuracies (∼ 55% and 57.5%). Some supplemental outcomes are shown only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Supplemental figure-only numeric values were not reconstructed; the CIFAR-100 AlexNet qualitative result is recorded in R9.

untested.parts: No random-label versus natural-label training and held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
Does not test FCNs learning sparse local connections from scratch or isolate how much of the CNN advantage comes from locality versus weight sharing. MNIST and SVHN are not tested.
Using both Adam and SGD to demonstrate the architectural result does not provide the controlled optimizer comparison and tuning analysis specified by V4.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted large-batch recipes.
No controlled dropout comparison or dropout–augmentation–weight-decay interaction.
No magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: VanillaCNN on CIFAR-10 with Adam: eFCNs improve after initialization, outperform the standard FCN, and at some relaxation times exceed the best CNN accuracy. This is a separate optimizer condition absent from the rows, not merely unextracted figure-only numbers.
missing.locator: Supplement B; Figure 10 left and caption

missing.what: Local-block ablation: off-local blocks alone perform poorly, but combining them with local blocks improves accuracy when constraints are relaxed early enough. This directly bears on the contribution of locality and complementary nonlocal connections.

Weight-space interpolation between CNN and eFCN solutions yields higher test accuracy than either endpoint in the reported cases; output-space interpolation yields still larger gains. These qualitative results are omitted despite rows_left_out declaring no omitted result rows.

record.verdict_notes: This study is explicitly an original source for V3; labels are therefore empty. Its CNN-initialized FCNs matching or exceeding CNNs instantiate an exception already included in V3. All assessments use only the supplied text; precise figure-only values were not reconstructed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
The study tests embedded CNN checkpoints trained further as FCNs, but not FCNs learning sparse local connections from scratch or initialized from a trained CNN and then held at the CNN solution.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: eFCN (VanillaCNN embedded at relax time tw = 0)
rows.operation_detail: Embedded a CNN checkpoint in FCN space and continued training without convolutional constraints.

conditions.value: SGD, learning rate 0.01, minibatch size 250; no momentum or weight decay

rows.baseline: standard FCN: ∼ 55% in the protocol description; Fig. 3 text gives 57.5%
rows.note: The text compares this embedded, untrained CNN prior with the standard FCN and says it performs much better.
rows.check: The untrained convolutional initialization improves FCN accuracy to about 62.5% versus 57.5%, but remains below the CNN's approximately 72%. It closes only part of the architecture gap; it is not initialization from a trained CNN.

conditions.value: SGD, learning rate 0.01, minibatch size 250; no momentum or weight decay

rows.value: ∼ 55% in the protocol description; 57.5% in Section 4.1
rows.note: The paper gives two different approximate FCN accuracies in the supplied text; both are retained as stated.
rows.check: Interpret jointly with R5: the standard FCN performs substantially worse than the CNN. Preserve the distinction between approximately 55% final accuracy in the protocol and 57.5% in the best-accuracy comparison; the text does not establish that these are identical summaries.

rows.subject: eFCNs (VanillaCNN checkpoints embedded at intermediate relax times)
rows.stage_stated: CNN checkpoint training followed by 100 epochs of FCN-space training
rows.operation_detail: Relaxed the convolutional constraints at an intermediate training time, then continued training in FCN space.

conditions.value: SGD; learning rate 0.01 after embedding; minibatch size 250; no momentum or weight decay

rows.value: eFCN reaches and exceeds the CNN's final test accuracy
rows.note: The paper states the intermediate relaxation result qualitatively and does not give a precise accuracy here.
rows.check: The result directly demonstrates V3's CNN-initialization exception: intermediate-relaxation eFCNs exceed their source CNN's final accuracy.

rows.subject: eFCNs (all tested relax times)
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy trajectories after relaxing CNN constraints at multiple saved training times.
rows.value: test accuracy increases monotonously in time for all tw values
rows.note: The text reports the trend across all relax times but does not provide individual plotted values.
rows.check: Increasing accuracy during eFCN training alone does not measure the CNN–FCN performance comparison named by V3. Figure 2's caption says CIFAR-100, conflicting with the surrounding CIFAR-10 experimental description; flag this as an apparent caption error.

rows.subject: eFCNs (VanillaCNN checkpoints embedded at multiple relax times)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the ratio of off-local weight norm to total weight norm after eFCN training.
rows.note: This measurement tracks persistence of locality but is not itself a test-error or generalization-gap measure.
rows.check: The off-local weight ratio measures persistence of locality, not the test-error advantage attributable to locality. It is contextual mechanistic evidence and cannot establish V3 by itself.

rows.subject: eFCNs (VanillaCNN checkpoints embedded at multiple relax times)
rows.operation_detail: Measured training-loss gradient norm and top Hessian eigenvalue before and after eFCN training.
rows.measure: training-loss gradient norm and top Hessian eigenvalue
rows.value: after eFCN training, these indicators plummet by an order of magnitude
rows.note: These are landscape measurements, not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure or gap-ranking comparison specified in V7.
rows.check: Gradient norm and the largest Hessian eigenvalue measure landscape geometry. They neither compare architectural generalization directly nor implement V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure and gap-ranking analysis.

relation.reason: Own experiments compare CNNs, standard FCNs and embedded FCNs, directly testing V3's architecture advantage and initialization exception.

tranche.reason: CNN-to-FCN embedding and timed constraint relaxation directly investigate the architecture/generalization question through a different intervention from training architectures from scratch.
